COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
C482 No. 1415 of 2023
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 Mr. Dharmendra Barthwal, Advocate, for the
applicant.
Mr. V.K. Gemini, Deputy A.G., for the State
of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Himanshu Yadav, Advocate, for
respondent No.2.
This is a second phase of litigation by way of
C-482 Application. Almost the circumstance of the
contest happens to be the same, wherein, the
present applicant / husband puts a question to the
summoning order of 19th January, 2022, as it was
passed by the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, in
Criminal Case No.57 of 2022, State Vs. Bhupendra
Singh Bisht @ Mohit, for the alleged involvement
of the present applicant for commission of the
offence under Sections 323, 427, 504 and 506 of the
IPC, in which, the present applicant has been
summoned by the Court of Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Nainital, by an order dated 19
th January,
2022.
This Court earlier made an effort for
mediation and attempted to make them understand
to revive back the matrimonial relationship, but
owing to certain inevitable misunderstandings, the
matrimony could not be revived.
Consequently, the C-482 Application has
been preferred along with the Compounding
Application No. 1 of 2023, where the parties have
unanimously resolved, that they would be initiating
the proceedings under Section 13-B of the Hindu
Marriage Act, for dissolution of their marriage and
for the grant of permanent alimony, which has been
settled would be amounting to Rs.43 lacs, but the
modality of its payment has yet to be considered by
the Family Court before whom the proceedings
under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, is to
be drawn.

They have agreed that the visitation right
with the applicant will continue to meet his
daughter as per the time schedule given in the terms
of settlement, which are extracted hereunder :-
 "That during pendency of trial the parties
have reached into amicable settlement which are
being stated herein under as follows:-
a) The parties agree that they would jointly
prefer a proceeding for grant of mutual divorce
under section 13 (B) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
before the competent Family Court.
b) As regard the permanent alimony to be
paid to the wife in lieu of mutual divorce, the
parties agree that the house of the husband situated
at Dehradun would be sold. The proceeds of the
sale so received from selling the house would be
first set off against the Home loan pertaining to the
said house amounting Rs. 43 lakh approx. and the
remaining amount of the proceeds of the sale would
be credited to the Savings bank account of
respondent no. 2 which will form the permanent
alimony of respondent no. 2 in lieu of mutual
divorce.
c) It has further been decided between the
parties that the applicant father would have
visitation right and can visit and meet the daughter
of the parties anytime, any day between 10.00 AM
to 05.00 PM".
The parties are present in persons. They
have been duly identified by their respective
counsels, coupled with the fact, that the parties have
agreed with the terms of compromise as extracted
above, and they have now resolved to severe their
matrimonial relationship by resort to the
proceedings under Section 13-B of the Hindu
Marriage Act, subject to the terms and conditions as
extracted above.
In order to lessen the burden of the litigation
between the parties, this C-482 Application, would
stand disposed of in terms of the settlement as
referred to hereinabove as detailed in para 9 of the
C-482 Application, and as a consequence to which,
the C-482 Application would stand disposed of

resulting into quashing of the proceedings of
Criminal Case No.57 of 2022, State Vs. Bhupendra
Singh Bisht @ Mohit, pending consideration before
the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Nainital.
However, having quashed the criminal
proceedings, the issues inter se between them as per
the terms of the settlement, could be more
effectively ventured to be made by the Family
Court before who the proceedings under Section
13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, is to be drawn.
Subject to the above, the C-482 Application
stands closed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Dated 17.07.2023
Shiv
